description: The questions waiting for you under your own posts. Fetches a creator's recent posts, reads the comments on each, and returns them grouped under the post they were left on — every comment with a stable id, and the ones that look like questions or requests flagged and sorted to the top. This FINDS and helps you DRAFT answers; it cannot post them: this tool sends nothing, and a reply is only ever posted after the user confirms its exact text — never promise the user a reply will go out on its own. `since` filters on the POST's date, not the comments'. `limit` caps how many posts are opened. Pair it with show_audience_replies to lay the drafts out for triage. Costs 2 nooticr credits for the post list plus 2 per post opened — 14 credits at the default of 6 posts. Use when the job is to answer people; search_mentions is for what strangers say elsewhere.

commentsPerPost.description: Comments to read per post (default 20, max 50).

limit.description: Posts to open (default 6, max 12). Each one is a comment fetch, so this is the price.

platform.description: Platform. Defaults to tiktok, so SET IT whenever the user named a network — otherwise a question about X, LinkedIn or Reddit is silently answered with TikTok data, and an empty result looks like the account does not exist. Accepts what get_user_posts does: tiktok, instagram, youtube, douyin, xiaohongshu, twitter, bilibili, linkedin, reddit, weibo.

since.description: Only POSTS published on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD. It windows the posts, not the comments — comment dates are fabricated as 'now' on most networks and cannot be filtered on. Ignored where the platform returns no post dates either.

name: answer_my_audience

byCategory.description: Flagged against unclear, as the view's filter chips.

evidenceFrom.description: The cheap calls this was assembled from.

frameIndex.description: Where each returned frame sits in the video.

guidance.description: What to do with this payload, in prose. Read it: it is the instruction, not a summary.

cached.description: true when the answer was served from the server's cache, at no cost.

charged.description: false when the call was refused before anything was debited.

mode.description: Always "evidence": this payload is material you have still to read.

posts.description: The posts of this run, flattened for the card view.

postsChecked.description: Posts whose comments were actually read.

repliesCanBeSent.description: Always false: answer_my_audience posts nothing, so the drafts this produces are for a person to paste in themselves, or to send through draft_comment_reply and post_comment_reply after confirming the text.

since.description: The date window asked for, if any.

sinceApplied.description: False when the platform returned no dates, so the window could not be honoured.

term.description: The creator, as @handle — what the view puts in its header.

id.description: Addressable, and stable across calls — pass it back to show_audience_replies. Built from the platform's own comment id, or from a fingerprint of post, author and text where there is none. Not the positional scheme search_mentions uses, whose ids move when the paging or window changes.

postedAt.description: Null wherever the date could not be believed. Most networks stamp every comment with the moment of the fetch, so anything indistinguishable from now is dropped rather than repeated as fact.

signals.description: Which phrasing test matched, so the flag can be argued with.

wantsReply.description: True when it reads like a question or a request.

commentSample.description: The replies themselves, when they were read. Someone answering "same here, this is exactly my problem" under another person's thread is a better find than the thread — the permalink to quote is still this post's.

commentsRead.description: How many replies were read under this post. 0 means the thread would not open — not that nobody replied. Absent when nothing tried.

externalUrl.description: Permalink — the URL to feed back into another tool.

threads.description: Comments grouped under the post they were left on.

unavailable.description: Posts whose comments could not be read, with the reason.

wantsReplyCount.description: How many carry a reply signal. A sort, not a verdict.

title: Answer My Audience
